name: Non-Amazon AI audiobook proofing and finishing service for indie authors
buyer: Self-published authors with a backlist who cannot afford human narration and want audiobooks outside Amazon
pain: Human narration averages about $150/hour on ACX, so an 8-hour book costs over $1,000. Developer TTS tools leave chapter splitting, voice assignment and audio assembly to the author.
wedge: A done-for-you service that fixes pronunciation of names and jargon, checks chapters, and delivers upload-ready files for platforms that accept third-party files, such as YouTube, direct sales and Kobo.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: Using AI voices plus a done-for-you proofing pass at a flat $149-199 per book (an estimate) against human narration of about $150/hour times 8 hours.
scan1Edge.falsifier: Authors comparing against the $99 ElevenLabs plan plus their own labor, not human narration, would see the entrant as more expensive, and there would be no cash edge.

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: Price is the midpoint of an estimated $149-199 per book. Margin is the midpoint of the 40-60% estimate after voice costs. Each book needs listening QA time.

majorUncertainty: Whether authors will pay $149-199 for proofing when ElevenLabs sells the whole flow itself and the main distribution channel restricts third-party files.
unknowns: The author DIY time estimate of 20-30 hours is unsourced
No firm complaint thread was found
Which platforms accept third-party AI-narrated files
Voice licensing terms for resale services
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Depends on ElevenLabs or other TTS voice providers. Distribution channels restrict third-party AI-narrated files, and voice consent and AI-disclosure rules are shifting.
